findings.claim: A sweeper report that names a well-formed 40-hex commit which does not exist in the repository fails in git.Parent or git.Message. That is returned as a plain error, so it exits 1 and not 2. The docs say a refused report exits 2 and 'any other failure' exits 1, so a sweeper who names a nonexistent commit is not classed as a refused report. The effect is a wrong exit code only; nothing is stored and there is no security impact.

evidence: Read the full diff (lines 1-1345) in two pages.
Read engine/review/rolerecords.go:259-354 in the worktree: the commit is shape-checked with gitobject.IsName, so no flag injection reaches git.

The default role path in runReviewRecord keeps the order of checks and the required flags (--feature, --base, --head, --rows); only an accepted --role flag is added. TestRecordWithRoleReviewerIsReviewRecordByteForByte covers the unchanged default.
--rows with a non-reviewer role, unknown or empty roles, and --role on other verbs are all rejected with exit 1, and tests pin each case.

Sweep and record exit codes match the documented contract (0 stored, 2 refused or a check that did not run, 1 usage). The lock, copies and PATH wiring sit in the composition root. The review path uses no exec or net imports beyond the existing analyzers.
